{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZhQHZA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhDIQHs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 43, "title": "Serialize SH-2 and on-chip DMA video-memory writes into B-bus word phases", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At main revision `580a451e042591acdf2ce1a49b538a440a09b35b`, inspection shows that `CpuBus::buffered_external_write` divides writes only according to the SH7604 BSC width. The default CS2 interface is 32 bits, so a video-memory longword becomes one scheduled width-4 transfer. Its completion calls `Bus::write::<4>`, publishing both device words together.

Consequently, the scheduler cannot represent a completed first video-memory word while the second remains pending. Ordinary VRAM, framebuffer and palette uploads can therefore have incorrect publication and ownership boundaries relative to drawing and display acquisition. Both SH-2s and their on-chip DMACs use this path.

Issue #37 introduced separate B-bus memory-read phases and explicitly deferred writes. Issue #41 already provides sound-RAM word completions; preserve that implementation and its evidence.

## Expected outcome

Implement downstream word phases for scheduled CPU/on-chip-DMAC writes to VDP1 VRAM and the CPU-accessible draw framebuffer, VDP2 VRAM and VDP2 CRAM, including their existing documented aliases.

A legal longword write must retain its accepted payload and publish its two 16-bit device transfers separately. Byte and word writes retain their requested strobes. Each phase must respect the target's ownership and access grants. Preserve the distinction between CPU-facing transaction width, buffer acceptance and downstream publication.

Primary contract:

- [SCU User’s Manual ST-097-R5](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-097-R5-072694.pdf), §3.2, printed pp.43–45, figs.3.6–3.8: the 32-bit transfer is divided into two 16-bit transfers at the B-bus device interface. These figures describe DMA transfers and establish interface granularity, not an exact CPU-write waveform.
- [SCU Final Specifications ST-210](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-210-110194.pdf), §3 item32, printed p.9: CPU writes preserve their requested access size. Reconcile applicable restrictions, including item03; do not generalize memory conversion into permissive MMIO accesses.
- [SH7604 Hardware Manual](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/sh7604.pdf), §7.11.2, printed pp.210–211: CPU/DMAC buffer acceptance precedes external write completion; dependent external reads drain pending writes.
- [VDP1 §2.1](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp1/hon/p02_10.htm) and [VDP2 §3.3](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p03_30.htm): target-memory ownership and display-period access allocation.

Document independently derived transaction examples before using implementation output as an oracle. Distinguish specified granularity from deterministic bridge-phase conventions and unmeasured electrical timing.

## Context and reproduction

Relevant paths are `src/bus/transactions.rs::buffered_external_write`, `grant_cpu_beat`, `complete_bus_transaction`, `src/bus.rs::CpuBus::external_write`, and `src/onchip/bsc.rs::Bsc::bus_width`.

A focused native reproduction should enqueue a longword to video memory using default CS2 settings and observe the pending transfer and publication boundaries. The inherited path schedules width 4 and performs one four-byte publication. Add a distinguishing regression that observes the first word completed while the second remains unchanged, then its later completion.

Keep this task focused on video-memory writes. Preserve existing read bridging, SCU DMA/DSP transfers, sound-RAM allocation, MMIO contracts, cache coherence policy and debugger inspection. Do not obtain serialization merely by changing the CPU-facing BSC width.

Technical assumptions in this AI-authored task may be corrected using exact primary references and documented rationale in the source Issue. Such corrections require no human confirmation and must preserve meaningful independent validation and the fixed campaign goal.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement retained, separately completed video-memory word phases for both SH-2 CPUs and both on-chip DMACs. Longwords publish two words; byte/word writes do not widen or disturb neighboring bytes. Preserve supported width/endian behavior, architectural alignment checks, memory geometry and aliases.
- [ ] Add independent native vectors covering every scoped endpoint, both processors, both DMACs, longword and 16-byte DMA units, byte lanes and word controls. Author literal expected addresses, payloads, ordering and deadlines without production transfer/grant helpers supplying the oracle.
- [ ] Exercise VDP1 drawing ownership and VDP2 display grants, including a delayed second phase and before/equal/after display-acquisition boundaries. Demonstrate partial publication, retained write data, no replay of completed words, dependent-read draining, correct buffer backpressure and appropriate progress of independent work. Preserve CPU-facing UBC observation sizes and counts.
- [ ] Test queued, accepted and partially completed writes across power/manual CPU resets and system reset. Preserve documented reset drains, already completed words and peer state; canceled work must not publish later. Verify identical records and traces across advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000 and passive debugger previews.
- [ ] Preserve documented early on-chip-DMAC buffer acceptance and completion/interrupt behavior; do not move its existing TE/IRQ boundary to final device publication merely to simplify the implementation. Retain SCU final-destination-before-end-IRQ behavior and #41 sound-memory allocation/reset regressions without duplicate internal writes.
- [ ] Add an original MIT-licensed, reproducible SH-2 guest that performs timed longword uploads and computes readback/FRT records, exercising both CPUs and on-chip DMA. Execute identical bytes in native Machine tests and rebuilt production browser Wasm under `/saturn-rust/`. Include a rendering assertion that distinguishes the two publication boundaries, changed-payload and omitted-write controls, and repeated cold boots. Host code must not supply running guest results or pixels.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the new distinguishing native regression and guest validation reject the inherited atomic video-write path. Record actual results and update the conformance matrix and validation record with precise specification, implementation and test links. Any necessary historical timing-fixture adjustment must retain its substantive assertions and explain the independently derived correction.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native and Wasm Clippy with warnings denied, all registered fixture/media reproduction checks, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, and the complete extended `npm run test:browser`. Preserve Star Collector, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab, existing audio, backup, input and privacy coverage; skip no required tests.

This is a partial #17 increment. Remaining CPU/peripheral semantics, multiprocessor and board timing/reset behavior, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integration acceptance remain mandatory. Passing this task does not establish broad commercial-game compatibility, which remains unverified.

## Optional validation

None required. No personal firmware, commercial media, physical console, human testing/approval or live Pages inspection is needed.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
